Check whether the laptop is used on a soft surface that blocks the vents.
Run the manufacturer's hardware diagnostics, including the fan and thermal tests.
Compare the BIOS and thermal driver versions with the approved versions in the company catalog.

steps: Use the laptop on a hard, flat surface and keep the vents clear; do not open the chassis.
End or fix a runaway process using KB-0030.
Install the approved BIOS and thermal-management updates from the company portal.
If diagnostics report a fan or thermal failure, raise a hardware repair request.
Stop using the device and escalate if it is too hot to touch, shuts down repeatedly, or smells of burning.

escalation_criteria: Escalate immediately for burning smells, battery swelling or repeated thermal shutdowns; otherwise escalate if diagnostics fail.
prevention: Keep firmware current, avoid soft surfaces, include thermal checks in hardware health reviews.

title: Computer slow or freezing because memory is low
symptoms: Windows warns that the computer is low on memory.
The machine becomes unusable by the afternoon until I restart.
Task Manager shows memory near 100% with a few apps open.
common_error_codes: Your computer is low on memory
root_cause: Too many applications or browser tabs, a memory leak in an application or extension, too little RAM for the workload, or faulty memory.
diagnostic_steps: Open Task Manager > Processes and sort by Memory; record the largest consumers.
Check Task Manager > Performance > Memory for committed memory and installed RAM.
Compare installed RAM with the documented requirements of the user's main applications.
If crashes also occur, run Windows Memory Diagnostic (`mdsched.exe`) when directed by support.

steps: Save work, close or restart the application that is leaking memory, and remove problem browser extensions.
Disable unnecessary startup apps in Task Manager > Startup apps and restart the device.
Install approved application and OS updates.
If RAM is insufficient for the role, raise a hardware request for an upgrade or a different device.
If the memory diagnostic reports errors, raise a hardware repair request.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if memory diagnostics report errors, crashes continue after cleanup, or many users on the same model are affected.
prevention: Size devices to role requirements, keep applications updated, review startup apps.

title: Laptop disk full or drive failure warning
symptoms: Windows says the disk is almost full and I can't save files.
The laptop is very slow and shows a disk warning.
A message says the hard drive may be failing.
root_cause: Temporary files, downloads, caches or locally synced cloud files filled the system drive, or the drive is failing (SMART or disk errors).
diagnostic_steps: Check Settings > System > Storage for free space and the largest categories.
Look for large folders such as Downloads and locally kept OneDrive files.
Run manufacturer diagnostics and note any SMART warning.
Check Event Viewer > Windows Logs > System for disk errors (for example Event ID 7 or 153).

steps: Run Storage Sense or Disk Cleanup and clear temporary files; delete personal downloads only after the user confirms.
Use OneDrive Files On-Demand ('Free up space') for files that are safely in the cloud.
Never delete system or program folders to free space.
If SMART or disk errors are present, back up data immediately and raise a hardware replacement request.
Verify at least 15% free space and no new disk errors.

escalation_criteria: Escalate immediately if a drive failure is predicted or data may be lost; escalate if the disk fills again quickly.
prevention: Enable Storage Sense, use Files On-Demand, monitor disk health in device management.

title: USB keyboard or mouse not recognised, or keyboard types wrong characters
symptoms: My USB keyboard or mouse is not detected when I plug it in.
Some keys type different symbols than the ones printed on them.
The touchpad or keyboard stopped responding but an external device works.
common_error_codes: Unknown USB Device (Device Descriptor Request Failed)
root_cause: A faulty port, cable, receiver or unpowered hub, USB power management, a driver problem, or the wrong input language or keyboard layout.
diagnostic_steps: Try another USB port directly on the laptop and test the device on another computer.
Check Device Manager > Keyboards, Mice and Universal Serial Bus controllers for warnings.
For wrong characters, check Settings > Time & language > Language & region for the active keyboard layout.
Check whether Filter Keys or Num Lock is changing key behaviour, or whether the touchpad was disabled with a function key.

steps: Connect the device directly to the laptop instead of an unpowered hub.
In Device Manager, uninstall the device with the warning and reconnect it so Windows reinstalls it.
Set the correct keyboard layout and remove layouts the user does not need.
Turn off Filter Keys if enabled, and re-enable the touchpad from settings or the function key.
If the peripheral or built-in keyboard has failed, raise a hardware request for replacement or repair.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if the built-in keyboard or touchpad has failed, multiple ports fail, or a fleet-wide driver issue appears.
prevention: Use approved peripherals and powered hubs, standardise keyboard layouts in device setup.

title: Mailbox full: cannot send, or messages bounce
symptoms: Outlook says my mailbox is full and I can't send emails.
Colleagues tell me their emails to me are bouncing.
I get a daily warning that my mailbox is almost full.
root_cause: The mailbox has reached its storage quota, usually because of large attachments, retained deleted items or no archive policy. A 5.2.2 bounce received by a sender means the recipient's mailbox is full.
diagnostic_steps: Check the mailbox size in Outlook (File > Info > Mailbox settings) or in webmail.
Determine whether the bounce refers to the user's own mailbox or to a recipient.
Check whether Online Archive and retention policies are enabled for the user.

steps: Empty Deleted Items and Junk, and remove or save large attachments to OneDrive or SharePoint.
Move older mail to the Online Archive according to the retention policy.
Do not delete items under retention or legal hold.
If the role genuinely needs more space, submit a quota increase request through the service portal.
Send a test message and confirm it is delivered.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if a shared or executive mailbox is full, mail flow is blocked for many users, or retention holds prevent cleanup.
prevention: Enable Online Archive, share links instead of attachments, review mailbox size warnings early.

title: Outlook disconnected, stuck on 'Trying to connect' or repeatedly asking for a password
symptoms: Outlook shows Disconnected and no new mail arrives.
Outlook keeps prompting for my password after I changed it.
Webmail works but desktop Outlook does not sync.
root_cause: A network or VPN problem, an expired sign-in token or cached old password, Work Offline being enabled, a corrupted Outlook profile or OST file, or a service outage.
diagnostic_steps: Check the Outlook status bar and the service-health page for mail incidents.
Confirm webmail access works with the same account.
Check whether the password was changed recently.
Check that Send/Receive > Work Offline is not enabled.

steps: Turn off Work Offline and confirm the network or VPN connection.
Sign out of the Office account and sign in again; remove outdated Outlook entries from Windows Credential Manager if prompted by support.
Run Quick Repair for Microsoft 365 Apps from Settings > Apps.
If the issue persists, have support create a new Outlook profile so the mailbox cache is rebuilt.
Confirm new mail and calendar items synchronise.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if many users are disconnected, the service-health page shows an incident, or a shared mailbox is affected.
prevention: Keep Office updated, use modern authentication, and update credentials on all devices after a password change.

title: Windows Update fails to install or keeps rolling back
symptoms: Windows Update fails every time with an error code.
An update installs, then rolls back after restart.
The device is reported as missing important updates.
root_cause: Insufficient disk space, the device being unable to reach the update service or WSUS (network, proxy or off-VPN), corrupted component store, a pending restart, or managed update policy.
diagnostic_steps: Record the error code from Settings > Windows Update > Update history.
Check free disk space on the system drive.
Check whether the device is managed by Intune or WSUS and whether it must be on the corporate network or VPN.
Run the Windows Update troubleshooter where available.

steps: Restart the device once to clear pending operations, then retry the update.
Free disk space (see KB-0045) and connect to the corporate network or VPN if the device uses WSUS.
Have support run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` followed by `sfc /scannow` from an elevated terminal.
Do not download update packages from third-party websites.
Retry and confirm the update appears as installed in Update history.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if updates fail after DISM/SFC, a security update is overdue on many devices, or the device cannot boot after an update.
prevention: Keep free space above 15%, connect regularly to the corporate network, use managed update rings.

title: Signed in with a temporary profile or profile fails to load
symptoms: After signing in, my desktop files and settings are missing.
Windows says I have been signed in with a temporary profile.
My settings reset every time I sign in.
common_error_codes: You've been signed in with a temporary profile
The User Profile Service failed the sign-in
root_cause: The user profile is corrupted, the profile registry entry is damaged, the disk has errors, or security software locked the profile during sign-in.
diagnostic_steps: Record the exact message and time; check whether other users on the device are affected.
Check Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Application for User Profile Service events.
Check disk space and disk health (see KB-0045).

steps: Warn the user not to save work in the temporary profile, because it is deleted at sign-out; save to OneDrive instead.
Restart the device once and sign in again.
If the temporary profile persists, have support repair the profile registry entry using the supported procedure, or create a new profile.
Restore the user's files from OneDrive or the old profile folder after the profile works.
Confirm the profile loads normally after two sign-ins.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if data may be lost, many users are affected, or disk errors are found.
prevention: Use OneDrive Known Folder Move, monitor disk health, avoid manual profile deletions.

title: Camera or microphone not working in Teams or other meeting apps
symptoms: Others cannot hear me in meetings, but my headset works for music.
My camera shows a black screen or is not detected in meetings.
The meeting app says it cannot find a microphone.
common_error_codes: Camera is being used by another app
root_cause: Windows privacy settings block access, another application is using the device, the wrong device is selected in the meeting app, or a driver, dock or client version problem.
diagnostic_steps: Check Settings > Privacy & security > Camera and Microphone, and allow desktop apps access.
Check the device selected in the meeting app's settings and run its test call.
Close other apps that may be using the camera or microphone.
Check Device Manager > Cameras and Audio inputs for warnings.

steps: Allow camera and microphone access in Windows privacy settings.
Select the correct camera, microphone and speaker in the meeting app.
Close the app holding the device, or restart the meeting app.
Update the meeting client from the company portal; reconnect the headset or camera directly rather than through a dock.
Run a test call and confirm audio and video work.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if many users are affected after a client update, or the built-in camera or audio device has failed.
prevention: Keep meeting clients updated, use approved headsets and cameras, test devices before important meetings.

title: OneDrive or SharePoint files not syncing
symptoms: OneDrive has shown sync pending or processing changes for hours.
Files I save do not appear for my colleagues in SharePoint.
Some files show a red sync error.
root_cause: Network or proxy problems, the user signed out of OneDrive, invalid file names or overly long paths, files open in another app, a full storage quota, or edit conflicts.
diagnostic_steps: Click the OneDrive cloud icon and open View sync problems; record affected files and messages.
Confirm the user is signed in and can open OneDrive on the web.
Check file names for unsupported characters and very long paths.
Check the OneDrive storage quota.

steps: Pause and resume syncing, then sign in again if prompted.
Rename files with unsupported characters or shorten long paths; close files open in other apps.
Free space or request more storage if the quota is full.
Reset OneDrive only when IT instructs it, using the documented reset command.
For conflict copies, let the file owner decide which version to keep; do not delete either copy automatically.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if sync failures affect a team site for many users, data appears to be missing, or the service-health page shows an incident.
prevention: Use supported file names, keep the client updated, and share links instead of copies.

title: Password expired or needs to be reset
symptoms: Windows says my password has expired and must be changed.
I forgot my password after returning from leave.
My new password keeps being rejected.
common_error_codes: Your password has expired and must be changed
Password does not meet complexity requirements
The user name or password is incorrect
root_cause: The password reached its expiry age, the new password does not meet length, complexity or history rules, or the new password has not reached all devices.
diagnostic_steps: Verify the user's identity using the service desk's approved method; never ask for the current password.
Check that the account is not locked or disabled.
Check whether the user is registered for self-service password reset.
For domain-joined laptops, check whether the device is on the corporate network or VPN.

steps: Direct the user to the official self-service password reset portal from a trusted device.
On a domain-joined device, use Ctrl+Alt+Del > Change a password while connected to the network or VPN.
If self-service is not possible, have the service desk reset the password after identity verification and require a change at next sign-in.
Never send passwords by email or chat.
Remind the user to update the password on phones and other devices to avoid lockouts (see KB-0054).

escalation_criteria: Escalate if identity cannot be verified, the account is privileged, or there are signs of compromise.
prevention: Encourage self-service registration and send expiry reminders.

title: Domain account repeatedly locked out or disabled
symptoms: My account gets locked several times a day.
Since I changed my password I keep getting locked out.
Windows says my account has been disabled after I returned from leave.
common_error_codes: The referenced account is currently locked out
Your account has been disabled. Please see your system administrator.
root_cause: Old credentials saved on a phone, second laptop, mapped drive, scheduled task or Wi-Fi profile keep failing after a password change. A disabled account usually follows HR or contract status changes. Lockouts can also come from attack attempts.
diagnostic_steps: Verify the user's identity using the approved method.
Have support check domain controller Event ID 4740 for the lockout's caller computer.
List the devices and apps where the user is signed in and check for a recent password change.
For a disabled account, check HR or contract status with the manager.
Flag lockouts from unknown devices or external addresses to security.

steps: Unlock the account after identity verification.
Remove stale credentials: Windows Credential Manager entries, the phone mail account, mapped drives and saved Wi-Fi profiles.
Sign out of old sessions on other devices, then monitor for further lockouts.
For a disabled account, re-enable it only after manager or HR confirmation through the access workflow.
If the lockout source is unknown or external, escalate to security before unlocking again.

escalation_criteria: Escalate to security if lockouts come from unknown sources, many accounts are affected, or the account is privileged.
prevention: Update credentials on all devices after a password change, and alert on repeated lockouts.

title: MFA push notifications not received, or unexpected MFA prompts
symptoms: I don't receive the Authenticator push notification when signing in.
The approval request times out before my phone shows it.
I keep getting MFA approval requests that I did not start.
root_cause: The phone is offline, notifications are disabled or blocked by battery optimisation, the app is outdated, the phone's time is wrong, or registration is stale. Unexpected prompts can indicate that someone else has the password (MFA fatigue attack).
diagnostic_steps: Check the phone's connectivity, that notifications are enabled for the app, and that date and time are automatic.
Open the Authenticator app manually to see whether a request is pending.
Check whether the user recently changed phones.
For unexpected prompts, record the times and any location shown, and do not approve them.

steps: Use the one-time code shown in the Authenticator app as an alternative sign-in method.
Enable notifications and disable battery optimisation for the app; update it from the official app store.
Re-register the method in the security-information portal if needed (see KB-0017).
Never approve a prompt you did not start; report unexpected prompts to security immediately.
For suspected fatigue attacks, security resets the password, revokes sessions and reviews sign-in logs.

escalation_criteria: Escalate immediately to security for unexpected prompts, approved fraudulent prompts, or sign-ins from unknown locations.
prevention: Register a backup method, use number matching, and train users not to approve unexpected prompts.

title: Request access to an application, shared mailbox, group or site
symptoms: I need access to an application or site for my new role.
I get an access denied or request access message when opening a resource.
A new team member needs the same access as the rest of the team.
common_error_codes: You need permission to access this resource
root_cause: Access is granted through role-based groups that require owner or manager approval; the user is not yet a member of the required group.
diagnostic_steps: Identify the exact resource (application, shared mailbox, distribution list, SharePoint site or group) and the access level needed.
Identify the resource owner and whether a peer in the same role already has equivalent access.
Check whether an access request is already pending.

steps: Submit an Access Request in the service portal with the resource, access level, business justification and duration.
The resource owner or manager approves or rejects it in the workflow.
The identity team adds the user to the minimum approved group; do not grant individual or broad rights as a shortcut.
Ask the user to sign out and back in so the new group membership applies.
Verify access and record the approval in the ticket.
resolution.estimated_time: 5-15 minutes to submit; approval time varies

escalation_criteria: Escalate if access is needed urgently for a critical process, the owner is unknown, or the request exceeds the user's role.
prevention: Use role-based access packages for common roles and run periodic access reviews.

title: Suspected phishing email, or user clicked a link or entered credentials
symptoms: I received an email asking me to verify my password, and it looks suspicious.
An unexpected invoice or delivery attachment arrived from an unknown sender.
I clicked a link and entered my password before realising it was fake.
root_cause: A phishing message is trying to steal credentials or deliver malware. The risk depends on whether the user clicked, opened an attachment, entered credentials or approved an MFA prompt.
diagnostic_steps: Ask whether the user clicked a link, opened an attachment, entered credentials or approved an MFA request, and when.
Ask the user not to forward the email to colleagues.
Check whether other users received the same message.

steps: Report the email with the Report Phishing button, or forward it as an attachment to the security mailbox as the policy says, then delete it.
If credentials were entered, change the password immediately from the official portal and contact the service desk.
Security revokes active sessions, reviews sign-in logs and mailbox rules, and resets MFA if needed.
If an attachment was opened, disconnect the device from the network (Wi-Fi off or cable unplugged), leave it powered on, and contact security.
Security searches for and removes the same message from other mailboxes.

escalation_criteria: Escalate immediately to security if credentials were entered, an attachment was opened, an MFA prompt was approved, or many users received the message.
prevention: Run regular phishing awareness training and make the Report Phishing button easy to find.

title: Malware or ransomware alert on a device
symptoms: Endpoint protection says a threat was detected on my laptop.
A pop-up says a file was quarantined.
Files have strange extensions and there is a note asking for payment.
root_cause: Malicious software reached the device through a download, attachment, removable media or a compromised site. Ransomware encrypts files and may spread to network shares.
diagnostic_steps: Record the detection name, file path, time and action taken from the endpoint protection notification.
Ask whether files have been renamed or encrypted, or a ransom note has appeared.
Check whether other devices or shared drives show the same signs.

steps: For any sign of ransomware, disconnect the device from the network immediately, leave it powered on, and call the security incident line.
Do not pay, contact the attacker, or delete the ransom note.
Security isolates the device through endpoint detection and response, investigates and contains the spread.
After security clears the device, it is reimaged and files are restored from verified backups.
For a single quarantined detection with no further activity, keep the file quarantined, run a full scan and report it to security.

escalation_criteria: Escalate immediately to security for any ransomware sign, repeated detections, spread to shares or other devices, or disabled protection.
prevention: Keep endpoint protection healthy, patch promptly, back up regularly and train users on downloads and attachments.

title: Antivirus definitions out of date, or how to run a scan
symptoms: My antivirus says protection definitions are out of date.
How do I run a full antivirus scan on my laptop?
Can I change the time of the automatic scan?
root_cause: The device has been offline or off VPN, cannot reach the update service, or the security agent is unhealthy. Scan schedules are managed centrally.
diagnostic_steps: Check Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection updates for the last update time.
Check network and VPN connectivity.
Check the device's agent health in the endpoint-management console (support).

steps: Connect to the corporate network or VPN and select Check for updates.
Restart the device if the update still fails.
If the agent is unhealthy, have endpoint security reinstall it through managed deployment.
Never disable real-time protection to fix update or performance issues.
To scan on demand, use Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options; scheduled scan times are set by policy.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if many devices fail to update, the agent cannot be repaired, or protection has been disabled.
prevention: Connect devices to the network regularly and monitor agent health centrally.

title: Internal web application shows HTTP 500/403 errors or loops at sign-in
symptoms: The internal portal shows an error page when I sign in.
The application keeps redirecting and never loads.
The application is down for everyone in my team.
root_cause: A server-side application error or outage (500/503), a missing role or group (403), stale cookies or an expired single sign-on session (redirect loop), or an unsupported browser.
diagnostic_steps: Record the URL, time, error code and any correlation or request ID shown on the error page.
Check whether colleagues see the same error and check the service-status page.
Retry in a private (InPrivate/Incognito) window to rule out cached cookies.

steps: Clear the site's cookies or use a private window, then sign out of single sign-on and sign in again.
Use a supported browser version.
For HTTP 403, submit an access request for the application role (see KB-0056).
For HTTP 500/503 affecting several users, raise an incident for the application owner with request IDs and timestamps.
Verify the application loads and the original task can be completed.

escalation_criteria: Escalate if the application is down for many users, data was lost on submit, or the error affects a business-critical deadline.
prevention: Show request IDs on error pages, monitor application health, and document required roles.
